status.ready: Ready: the route is in place, waiting for people to use it

items.title: Test the catalogue with 5 to 8 people from at least four audiences who don't use GitHub
items.now: Personas and journeys are proto-personas, not yet tested with users. From 7.16.0 the research bundle is ready: a plan with tactical and strategic questions, an invitation to send by email, participant information, consent, a screener, session guides and a sign-up form. It needs facilitators and participants.
items.label: Help shape the catalogue

items.title: Measure the precision of each topic on a labelled sample, as was done for strategy and DAM tags
items.now: Topics are keyword leads (Browse by topic). Every project page now has 'Check a label', an issue form whose answers become the labelled sample.
items.label: Check a label

items.title: Ask organisations to check their profile and say whether the next steps are useful
items.now: Every organisation profile now has 'Check this profile', an issue form that names the organisation.
items.label: Check a profile

items.title: Check the catalogue manually with screen readers, magnifiers at 400% zoom and speech input
items.now: Automated checks pass (axe-core on every view, contrast in light and dark, widths from 320 pixels, keyboard tests). Manual testing hasn't been done.
items.label: Track the manual check

items.title: Publish an accessibility statement with known issues and a way to ask for help
items.now: The statement under About, Accessibility, now gives the tests and their dates, the known issues and an assisted route through the contact form; it is also docs/accessibility-statement.md.
items.label: Read the statement

items.title: Learn which hubs and questions people use, with their consent
items.now: The page has no analytics and its security policy blocks them, so nothing is tracked. The owner can see visits to the repository in GitHub's traffic insights; GitHub Pages offers no analytics.
items.label: Repository traffic (owner only)

items.title: Join projects to the datasets they publish or use in data catalogues (data.gov.uk, statistics.gov.scot, Data Map Wales, NHS catalogues)
items.now: The pan-UK view stops at code, not datasets (Data infrastructure, 'What this view needs').
items.label: Track the join

items.title: Add boundaries and locations so nations, authorities and councils can be shown on maps
items.now: No boundary data is held, so places are shown as lists and tables.
items.label: Track the maps

items.title: Collect GitHub feature settings (Issues, Projects, Wiki, Discussions) for every project, not a sample
items.now: Feature settings are an estimate from a random sample. The collector is a manual workflow in this repository; a person runs it with a token that can read the accounts.
items.label: Run the collector

items.title: Re-read GitHub so projects found since the catalogue was built are added
items.now: Done in 7.17.0: build/refresh/run.sh re-reads the sources, checks with git every repository a source drops, and re-measures activity. A person sets the date and reviews and commits the result.
items.label: The refresh, step by step

items.title: Link repositories to the systems they belong to
items.now: None of GTI, ANA or LIAH names systems or repositories yet, so these links wait for LIAH to hold real system records.
items.label: Track the link

items.title: A named team accepts ownership: answers issues, reviews pull requests and reviews the catalogue every quarter
items.now: Blocker B1 in the release readiness assessment. The GDS Way asks for review by someone other than the author.
items.label: Release readiness

items.title: Move the repository to its agreed home organisation
items.now: Blocker B2: gds-dtx is recommended, after its owners agree (ADR 0003).
items.label: Decision records

items.title: Switch on the repository's security settings: private vulnerability reporting, secret scanning with push protection, a ruleset for main, Actions limits and approval for outside contributors
items.now: Items 3 to 8 in the settings review. Until private vulnerability reporting is on, the Cabinet Office programme is the only private route for security reports.
items.label: Security settings (owner only)

items.title: Show the catalogue's address in the repository's About box
items.now: Done: the repository's website is https://cyberdudeuk.github.io/github-repos-asset-catalogue/ (read from GitHub on 4 November 2026).
items.label: Repository page

items.title: Create the Discussions category 'Feature assessment' so new GitHub features can be assessed
items.now: The form is ready in .github/DISCUSSION_TEMPLATE/feature-assessment.yml; it appears once the category exists with the slug feature-assessment.
items.label: Discussion categories (owner only)

items.title: Replace the public contact form with the team's private contact form
items.now: Messages in the GitHub contact form are public. Once the team has a private form (for example on GOV.UK Forms), set GHRAC_CONTACT_URL when building.
items.label: Deployment settings

items.title: Tag releases and publish release notes from one place
items.now: Blocker B10. Releases and their notes are in docs/releases.md, but no release is tagged on GitHub yet; automation here can't create releases.
items.label: Draft a release (owner only)

items.title: Ask GitHub Support to remove cached views of commits from before the history rewrites
items.now: The history was rewritten twice on 3 November 2026. Old commits can still be reached by their IDs through pull request references until GitHub Support removes them.
items.label: GitHub Support

items.title: Delete the stale branches gds-way-assessment, test-results-7.11.1, readme-assessment and roadmap-github
items.now: The first two hold code from before the public and internal split and fail the build; the other two were merged and are no longer needed. Deleting a branch is for a person to do.
items.label: Branches (owner only)

items.title: Serve a security.txt that points to the Cabinet Office vulnerability disclosure programme
items.now: The GDS Way asks for /.well-known/security.txt. A GitHub Pages project site can't serve files at the domain's root, so this needs a custom domain or a different host.
items.label: Track the decision

items.title: Data protection screening note, independent security review and a machinery-of-government content check before a wider release
items.now: Blockers B5, B6 and B11 in the release readiness assessment.
items.label: Release readiness

items.title: Create the labels the issue and discussion forms apply: contact, profile check, label check and roadmap
items.now: Read from GitHub on 4 November 2026: these four labels don't exist, so GitHub silently drops them and those issues can't be filtered or grouped in release notes.
items.label: Labels (owner only)

items.title: Require a person to approve each GitHub Pages deployment
items.now: The pages workflow publishes after its checks pass. A required reviewer on the github-pages environment makes GitHub itself wait for a person, as the catalogue's rules say. Do the same for the companion repository's government edition.
items.label: Environments (owner only)

items.title: Create a Q&A category in Discussions, with the slug q-a
items.now: Ask sends questions it can't answer to Discussions. The form is ready in .github/DISCUSSION_TEMPLATE/q-a.yml; it appears once the category exists. Answers can then be marked so the next person finds them.
items.label: Discussion categories (owner only)

items.title: Run the roadmap as a GitHub project board, with each item an issue
items.now: The roadmap-item form already opens issues. A board gives each a status, an owner and a date on GitHub, and sub-issues can link work to its item. Projects is switched on but unused.
items.label: Projects (owner only)

items.title: Signpost the two sister portals from the views where they help, keeping each distinct
items.now: Done in 7.16.0: 'Related elsewhere' on the data management wheel, data tools, catalogues and standards, and legacy views, each naming the portal and its status. The catalogue now uses the sister portals' keys: #dama=DM-GOV and #standard=dcat3 open the same area or standard here, and data/xref.json publishes its keys in the shape they use. A weekly check reads their manifests and the pages linked here.
items.label: This catalogue's shared keys
